The first lesson is to confirm actual data granularity before fixing architecture and capacity. The difference between hourly and 15-minute data affected storage, connectors, privacy, and testing. The second is to apply aggregation at the source whenever possible so that the most sensitive data does not leave the cooperative.

Governance must be implemented as an operational process rather than only as a document. Forms, expiry dates, decision logs, and revocation were necessary to apply the policy. Preserving time zones and provenance was also essential; an apparently minor transformation caused a one-hour shift.

Revocation and recovery tests should be part of the normal schedule. To scale VERDANT, certificate rotation should be automated, alerts should be reviewed periodically, and published indicators should clearly distinguish missing data from data deliberately withheld for privacy.
